✳ THE FAIRSHARE PROMPTDownload .txt ↗
Help me research class-action settlements I may qualify for using Fairshare:
https://github.com/oh-ashen-one/fairshare

Read README.md and AGENT_GUIDE.md first. If you can’t access them or search the live web, tell me before proceeding.

Start with a brief privacy explanation. Ask only for optional context: my country/state, products and apps I’ve used (up to 10 to start), approximate dates, and past employers if I want to include them. I can skip anything. Don’t ask for my name, address, account credentials, IDs, or financial details to start.

Research broadly, then verify each potential match against official settlement notices and administrator websites. Distinguish open claims from closed cases, investigations, and proposed settlements. Never guess eligibility, deadlines, or payouts.

Give me a dated, source-linked shortlist with eligibility rules, what matches, what’s unknown, deadlines, evidence needed, and official filing links. Explain search gaps. No matches is a valid result.

Help me understand and prepare truthful answers, but don’t submit, sign, accept terms, or contact anyone for me. I will review and file myself. Don’t save my personal details unless I ask, and never put them in Git or public search queries.
Then paste it into your agent.

LESS DATA. MORE CONTROL.

Your story isn’t
our business.

Fairshare has no intake form, account system, advertising trackers, or personal-data database. The website doesn’t receive the details you tell your agent.

Your AI provider is a separate choice. Cloud-powered agents may send prompts and files to their provider, even when the app runs locally. Check its settings. A fully local model offers more control, but web searches still leave your device.

Hosting providers may process standard request logs, such as IP addresses. Official claim sites have their own privacy policies. Read the full privacy notes ↗

FAIR QUESTIONS

A few things
to know.

Is this really free?

Yes. Fairshare is open source under the MIT license. We charge no subscription or claim fee and take no share of a payout. Your chosen AI provider may charge for its own tools or usage.

Will it find every settlement I qualify for?

No tool can promise complete coverage. Records are scattered, some aren’t public, and deadlines change. The guide asks your agent to search broadly, show sources and gaps, and treat a match as something to verify. No results doesn’t prove that no claim exists.

Does it work outside the United States?

The guide starts by asking your country. Its source directory is U.S.-focused. For other countries, your agent must identify local official sources, explain coverage limits, and avoid applying U.S. rules to your situation.

Do I have to share my name or personal documents?

No. A name usually isn’t needed for initial discovery. Start with products, approximate dates, and a state or region. Keep documents, claim IDs, identification numbers, and payment details out of the research conversation. Enter necessary sensitive information yourself only on a verified official claim site.

Will Fairshare file a claim for me?

No. Your agent can explain requirements and help you prepare truthful answers. You check the official notice, review any certification or release, and submit yourself. Never claim a purchase, loss, or experience you didn’t have.

What if my AI can’t open GitHub or browse?

Download the repository and give your agent README.md and AGENT_GUIDE.md. Live browsing is needed to verify current opportunities; without it, the agent should give you a research checklist instead of presenting stale information as current.

Is this legal advice or a guarantee of payment?

No. Fairshare is a research guide, not a law firm or settlement administrator. The administrator applies the settlement’s rules. Employment, releases, objections, and opt-outs can affect your rights; consult a qualified lawyer when you need advice about those decisions.
